title: Letter 26 — Why Pastors Are Shepherds
attribution_note: Letter 26 of 46 in the collection Letters Sent — see Letter 1 for provenance.

sections.heading: Why bishops and priests are called shepherds

pairs.en: Thou askest of me: wherefore are bishops and presbyters called shepherds?
Answer. For the same cause that herdsmen of cattle are called herdsmen, for that cause also are bishops and presbyters called shepherds.
Herdsmen are chosen by the whole village or hamlet, that they may pasture their cattle. So shepherds, bishops and presbyters are chosen of the Church, that they may pasture Christian souls.
Herdsmen pasture dumb cattle; but shepherds pasture the rational sheep of Christ — that is, men, redeemed by the Blood of Christ.
Herdsmen drive the cattle out into the field, unto the grass and unto a good pasture, and there feed them; but shepherds feed the sheep of Christ with the word of God and with the Holy Mysteries.

Herdsmen keep their flock and defend it from wolves and other beasts; but shepherds keep the flock of Christ's sheep and defend it from the devil, from demons, from heretics, from superstitious men and from other enemies — beasts of the soul.

Herdsmen, if any beast stray from the flock and go astray, seek it and drive it back into the flock; but shepherds, if any Christian stray from the true way, labour to turn him by the word of God and by exhortation, and to join him again unto the flock of Christ.

sections.heading: From the wilderness of the world unto the heavenly fold

pairs.en: Herdsmen pasture their flock in the field and in the steppe; but shepherds pasture the flock of Christ in the wilderness of this world.
Herdsmen drive their flock from the field into the houses of the masters; but shepherds send the flock of Christ beforehand from this world into the heavenly fold unto Christ the Lord.

Herdsmen for their labours, and for that they pasture, receive hire of the masters; but shepherds from Christ the Lord for their labours, and for that they pasture His flock, shall receive a reward — *“a crown of glory that fadeth not away”* [1 Peter 5:4].

Of the herdsmen, if they drive not some beast home, the masters demand: “Where is this and that beast of mine?” And of the shepherds, if any Christian perish and appear not in the heavenly fold, Christ the Lord will demand: “Where is such and such a sheep of Mine? Where is the sheep which I committed unto thee to pasture, and which thou receivedst whole in Baptism? Where is the sheep which I purchased not with silver and gold, but with Mine own Blood?”

A herdsman cannot say unto the master, “I know not where”; because he took the flock to keep it; and a shepherd cannot say unto Christ the Lord, “I know not where the sheep is”; because he was a watchman of the flock of Christ, and took the flock to keep it.

A herdsman is deprived of his hire by the master for the loss of a beast; and a shepherd is deprived by Christ of his reward for the destruction of a rational sheep, and is delivered over to punishment.

A herdsman is not guilty if not by his negligence, but in some other manner, a beast perish; and a shepherd shall not be guilty, and shall not be required of by Christ the Lord, if a Christian perish not by his negligence and want of watchfulness, but by his own carelessness and self-will — that is, when the shepherd taught, instructed, exhorted and showed him the pattern of good works, but he hearkened not unto him as unto his shepherd.
Behold, this is wherefore bishops and priests are called shepherds. Therefore consider this, and examine thyself, whether thou pasture the flock of Christ as is meet.
From this it followeth:
1) How wise and apt to teach shepherds must be.
2) With what virtues they must be adorned, that they may be an example unto the flock.
3) What care and concern they must have for the flock of Christ.
4) How diligently they must read Holy Scripture, whence instruction and teaching are drawn.
5) They must go into the shepherd's office not so much for bread as for the salvation of Christian souls.

6) When thou teachest men, labour that the parable be not said unto thee: *“Physician, heal thyself”* — and that thou hear not from God in thy conscience that which is said unto the sinner: *“What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth?* *Seeing thou hatest instruction, and castest my words behind thee”* [Psalm 50:16–17].

7) Better is it to please the one God than the whole world, and to do the will of the one God than the will of all men. No man shall defend thee before God when He shall judge thee; then shall princes and nobles, and the mighty, and kings hide themselves; thy conscience alone shall either justify thee or condemn thee. Remember this.

8) It is well also to *“please”* men, but *“for his good to edification”* [Romans 15:2]. But otherwise better is it to fall into the hatred of the whole world than to be deprived of the mercy of God and to fall under His righteous wrath. I will and I hold it thus. Let the whole world hate me, if it so please; only let the one God keep me in His mercy. Whom God loveth and keepeth in His mercy, him the wrath and hatred of the whole world and of all the devils can in no wise harm. For God is incomparably stronger and more sure than the whole world. Unto His command and will all things are subject. Consider this, and sink it deep into thine heart.
Be saved.
